## Purpose

This report records how the tmux configuration was reconstructed on a new
system and how the GitHub repository was made portable. Its purpose is to make
future installation, maintenance, and troubleshooting repeatable.

The target design uses [Oh My Tmux](https://github.com/gpakosz/.tmux) as the
base configuration, keeps personal options in `tmux.conf.local`, and lets Oh My
Tmux's built-in TPM integration manage
[tmux-menus](https://github.com/jaclu/tmux-menus).

## Initial system analysis

The system was inspected before modifying files. The relevant environment was:

| Component | Observed value |
| --- | --- |
| Operating system | CachyOS/Arch Linux derivative |
| tmux | 3.7c, installed through pacman |
| Login shell | fish |
| Terminal | Alacritty 0.17.0 |
| Outer `$TERM` | `xterm-256color` |
| Colour support | `COLORTERM=truecolor` |
| Display session | Wayland |
| Clipboard command | `/usr/bin/wl-copy` |
| tmux terminfo | `tmux-256color` available |
| UTF-8 locale | `en_GB.UTF-8` |
| Required commands | `awk`, `perl`, `grep`, `sed`, `git`, and `curl` present |
| Fonts | Noto Mono, Nerd Fonts, and Powerline symbols available |

No user tmux configuration, system `/etc/tmux.conf`, or running tmux server was
present. The installed package contained the tmux binary, manual, and licence,
but no distribution-specific configuration that needed to be preserved.

## What the original repository revealed

The original repository contained three important clues about the old setup:

1. `tmux.conf` was an absolute symlink to
   `/home/roblezno/oh-my-tmux/.tmux.conf`.
2. The TPM log referred to plugins under
   `/home/roblezno/.config/tmux/plugins`.
3. `tmux.conf.local` enabled `jaclu/tmux-menus` through Oh My Tmux's TPM
   integration.

This established the previous layout:

```text
~/oh-my-tmux/.tmux.conf
        ^
        |
~/.config/tmux/tmux.conf

~/.config/tmux/tmux.conf.local
~/.config/tmux/plugins/
```

### Repository defects

A fresh clone could not completely reproduce that layout:

- The absolute symlink only worked for the same username and directory.
- `plugins/tpm` and `plugins/tmux-menus` were recorded as gitlinks.
- No `.gitmodules` file provided URLs for those gitlinks.
- The generated `plugins/tpm_log.txt` file was committed.
- A normal clone therefore produced empty plugin directories which could stop
  Oh My Tmux from installing TPM correctly.

## Implemented repository architecture

Oh My Tmux was converted into a real, pinned Git submodule and the runtime
plugin directory was removed from version control:

```text
~/.config/tmux/
├── .git/
├── .gitignore
├── .gitmodules
├── README.md
├── docs/
│   └── configuration-process.qmd
├── oh-my-tmux/                 # Git submodule
├── plugins/                    # generated and ignored
├── tmux.conf -> oh-my-tmux/.tmux.conf
└── tmux.conf.local
```

The relative symlink makes the repository independent of the account's home
directory. Pinning Oh My Tmux as a submodule also makes upgrades explicit and
reproducible.

## Configuration process

### 1. Clone the personal repository

```sh
mkdir -p ~/.config
git clone https://github.com/Roblezno/tmux-conf.git ~/.config/tmux
cd ~/.config/tmux
```

### 2. Remove generated plugin state from Git

The broken gitlinks and historical TPM log were removed:

```sh
git rm -r plugins
printf 'plugins/\n' > .gitignore
```

TPM is responsible for recreating this directory at runtime.

### 3. Add Oh My Tmux as a real submodule

```sh
git submodule add https://github.com/gpakosz/.tmux.git oh-my-tmux
ln -sfn oh-my-tmux/.tmux.conf tmux.conf
```

The submodule was pinned at commit:

```text
58a3dcc0d718ec0fa1c0d5a2fddd640a1ad7a5b7
```

### 4. Enable clipboard integration

The system already had a Wayland session and `wl-copy`, so the local setting
was changed to:

```tmux
tmux_conf_copy_to_os_clipboard=true
```

Oh My Tmux then rewrites applicable copy-mode bindings to use `wl-copy`. For
example, the vi copy-mode `y` binding resolves to:

```text
send-keys -X copy-pipe-and-cancel wl-copy
```

### 5. Enable mouse mode by default

The local customization now contains:

```tmux
set -g mouse on
```

Mouse mode can still be toggled for the current server with `<prefix> m`.

### 6. Set the preferred editor

Fish universal exported variables were configured so `<prefix> e` opens
Neovim:

```fish
set -Ux EDITOR nvim
set -Ux VISUAL nvim
```

These variables are machine-specific and are not stored in this Git
repository. They must be set separately on each device.

### 7. First launch and plugin installation

Oh My Tmux found `set -g @plugin 'jaclu/tmux-menus'` in
`tmux.conf.local`. On first launch it created
`~/.config/tmux/plugins`, cloned TPM, and installed tmux-menus.

The same operation can be triggered manually from tmux with `<prefix> I`.

## Validation

The configuration was started on an isolated tmux socket so it could be tested
without affecting normal sessions:

```sh
tmux -L config-test \
  -f ~/.config/tmux/tmux.conf \
  new-session -d -s config-test
```

The following results were confirmed:

| Check | Result |
| --- | --- |
| Main config path | `~/.config/tmux/tmux.conf` |
| Plugin path | `~/.config/tmux/plugins` |
| Inner terminal type | `tmux-256color` |
| Primary prefix | `Ctrl-b` |
| Secondary prefix | `Ctrl-a` |
| Kanagawa status style | Loaded |
| TPM executable | Installed |
| tmux-menus | Installed and bound to `<prefix> \` |
| Clipboard copy | Bound to `wl-copy` |
| Mouse option | `on` |
| Editor variables | `EDITOR=nvim`, `VISUAL=nvim` |

The test server was stopped afterwards:

```sh
tmux -L config-test kill-server
```

A separate `git clone --recurse-submodules` test confirmed that the relative
symlink resolves and the pinned Oh My Tmux revision is checked out on a clean
machine.

## Installing on another device

### Arch Linux or derivative

```sh
sudo pacman -S tmux git wl-clipboard neovim
git clone --recurse-submodules \
  https://github.com/Roblezno/tmux-conf.git \
  ~/.config/tmux
tmux
```

For fish, restore the editor preference:

```fish
set -Ux EDITOR nvim
set -Ux VISUAL nvim
```

For an X11 session, install `xclip` or `xsel` instead of `wl-clipboard`. On
macOS, Oh My Tmux detects `pbcopy`.

### Existing clone missing the submodule

```sh
git -C ~/.config/tmux submodule update --init --recursive
```

### Existing tmux configuration

Before cloning, move any existing configuration to a backup location:

```sh
mv ~/.config/tmux ~/.config/tmux.backup
```

Also check for `~/.tmux.conf`, because tmux searches it before the XDG config.
If present, back it up or remove it after verifying it is no longer needed.

## Maintenance

### Change personal options

Only edit `tmux.conf.local`:

```sh
nvim ~/.config/tmux/tmux.conf.local
```

Reload from inside tmux with `<prefix> r`.

### Pull repository changes

```sh
git -C ~/.config/tmux pull --ff-only
git -C ~/.config/tmux submodule update --init --recursive
```

### Update the Oh My Tmux pin

```sh
git -C ~/.config/tmux/oh-my-tmux pull --ff-only
git -C ~/.config/tmux add oh-my-tmux
git -C ~/.config/tmux commit -m "chore: update Oh My Tmux"
```

### Manage TPM plugins

- `<prefix> I`: install missing plugins
- `<prefix> u`: update plugins
- `<prefix> Alt-u`: remove plugins no longer configured

The `plugins/` directory should remain ignored and must not be committed.

## Troubleshooting

### Confirm the config is discoverable

```sh
readlink -f ~/.config/tmux/tmux.conf
git -C ~/.config/tmux submodule status
```

From inside tmux:

```sh
tmux show-environment -g TMUX_CONF
tmux show-environment -g TMUX_PLUGIN_MANAGER_PATH
tmux show-messages
```

### Compare against an empty configuration

```sh
tmux -L clean-test -f /dev/null
```

If the issue is absent there, it is caused by user configuration or a plugin.

### Configuration does not reload

Use `<prefix> r`. If the tmux binary was upgraded while a server was running,
save work and restart all sessions:

```sh
tmux kill-server
tmux
```

### tmux-menus on tmux 3.7c

The plugin documents a tmux 3.7c bug where the left arrow cannot return to the
previous menu. Select the Back item and press Enter. The issue is fixed in tmux
3.8.

## Local Git history

The work was organized into commits covering the reproducible repository
layout, clipboard integration, default mouse mode, and documentation. Review
them with:

```sh
git -C ~/.config/tmux log --oneline --decorate
```

Publishing requires GitHub authentication and can be done with:

```sh
git -C ~/.config/tmux push origin main
```
